message.content:
### Tenant Rights in Texas (as of 2024) Below is a concise overview of key rights and protections afforded to tenants under Texas law. This list is not exhaustive; local ordinances or specific lease terms may add further rights or obligations. | Category | Key Rights | Notes | |----------|------------|-------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• Deposit must be returned within **30 days** after the tenant vacates, minus any lawful deductions. | Deductions may include unpaid rent, damage beyond normal wear, or cleaning costs. | | **Habitability** | • Landlord must maintain the premises in a safe, sanitary condition, complying with building, housing, and health codes.
• Repairs must be made promptly. | Tenants can withhold rent or repair and deduct if the landlord fails to act, but must follow proper procedures. | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease.
• Late fees are allowed only if stated in the lease and must be reasonable. | Texas law prohibits excessive late fees; they must be proportional to the rent amount. | | **Lease Termination** | • **Month-to-month** leases can be terminated by either party with **30 days’ written notice**.
• For fixed-term leases, the landlord may terminate early only for cause (e.g., nonpayment, violation of lease). | Notice must be in writing and delivered personally or via certified mail. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Tenants have the right to live without unreasonable interference from the landlord or other tenants. | Landlords cannot enter without notice unless in emergencies. | | **Landlord Entry** | • Landlord must give **at least 24 hours’ written notice** before entering, except in emergencies. | Entry is allowed for repairs, inspections, or showing the unit to prospective tenants. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (including public assistance). | This is enforced by the Texas Fair Housing Act and federal law. | | **Privacy** | • Landlord must respect tenant privacy; they cannot conduct surveillance or tamper with personal property. | Exceptions exist for security cameras in common areas, but not inside private units. | | **Maintenance of Common Areas** | • Landlord must keep common areas clean and safe. | Tenants can report issues; landlords must respond promptly. | | **Utilities** | • If utilities are included in rent, the landlord must ensure they are functional. | Tenants can request proof of utility service. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major defect, tenants may repair it themselves and deduct the cost from rent, following proper procedure. | Must provide written notice and keep receipts. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must provide a written notice (e.g., 3-day notice for nonpayment, 30-day notice for lease violations).
• Eviction must be pursued through court; landlords cannot forcibly remove tenants. | Tenants can contest eviction in court. | | **Right to a Written Lease** | • While not required, having a written lease clarifies rights and responsibilities. | Oral leases are enforceable but harder to prove. | | **Tenant’s Right to Repair** | • Tenants can repair and deduct if the landlord fails to fix major defects. | Must follow the “repair and deduct” process: written notice, repair, deduction from rent. | | **Right to Sublet** | • Tenants may sublet only with landlord’s written consent, unless the lease allows it. | Landlord cannot unreasonably deny consent. | | **Right to Access Records** | • Tenants can request records related to their tenancy (e.g., rent receipts, maintenance logs). | Landlord must provide them upon request. | --- #### Practical Steps for Tenants 1. **Read Your Lease Carefully** – Understand all terms, including rent amount, due dates, and notice periods. 2. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of notices, emails, and maintenance requests. 3. **Know the Notice Requirements** – For any lease termination or entry, ensure the landlord follows the required notice period. 4. **Report Issues Promptly** – Notify the landlord in writing of any maintenance problems. 5. **Seek Legal Advice if Needed** – If you face eviction or disputes, consult a tenant‑rights organization or attorney. --- #### Resources - **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)** – Provides tenant‑landlord guides and dispute resolution services. - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** – Offers information on fair housing and landlord‑tenant laws. - **Local Tenant‑Rights Organizations** – Many cities have nonprofits that offer free legal clinics and mediation services. --- **Disclaimer:** This information is intended as a general guide and does not constitute legal advice. Laws can change, and local ordinances may impose additional requirements. For specific legal questions, consult a qualified attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization.
